name: Ron DeSantis
role: Governor of Florida (2019-), former US Representative (2013-2018) and Navy JAG officer
summary: Ron DeSantis is a conservative Republican who, as a congressman, voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act and to restrict executive immigration relief, and as Florida governor has signed a six-week abortion ban, permitless concealed carry, universal school choice, restrictions on classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity, and an E-Verify and anti-smuggling immigration law.

sources.title: Roll-call votes of Rep. Ron DeSantis (FL-6), 113th-115th Congresses, Voteview (ICPSR 21318)
sources.author: Ron DeSantis
sources.usedFor: His votes on repealing the Affordable Care Act, the abortion bills, Defund Planned Parenthood, Concealed Carry Reciprocity, Keystone XL and natural-gas exports, and defunding executive immigration relief.

sources.title: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Heartbeat Protection Act (SB 300), Executive Office of the Governor, 13 April 2023
sources.author: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida
sources.usedFor: He signed SB 300 prohibiting abortion once a heartbeat can be detected.

sources.title: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Historic Bill to Protect Parental Rights in Education (HB 1557), press release of 28 March 2022 (copy on lobbytools.com)
sources.author: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida
sources.usedFor: He signed HB 1557, which bars classroom instruction on sexual orientation or gender identity in kindergarten to grade 3.

sources.title: FPC Applauds Florida Governor Ron DeSantis for Signing HB 543, Enacting Permitless Concealed Carry, Firearms Policy Coalition, 3 April 2023
sources.author: Firearms Policy Coalition
sources.usedFor: He signed HB 543, ending the licence requirement for carrying a concealed handgun.

sources.title: Ron DeSantis Signs Bill Expanding School Choice to All Florida Students, Reason, 27 March 2023
sources.author: Joe Lancaster
sources.usedFor: He signed HB 1, removing eligibility caps on Florida's school-choice scholarships.

sources.title: Gov. DeSantis signs controversial measure targeting immigration (SB 1718), WLRN, 10 May 2023
sources.author: WLRN / News Service of Florida
sources.usedFor: He signed SB 1718: E-Verify for employers of 25 or more, tougher smuggling penalties, hospital reporting, DNA samples from immigration detainees.

sources.title: Congressional Record, House floor speeches by Ron DeSantis, 2013-2016 (Stanford parsed Record)
sources.author: Ron DeSantis
sources.usedFor: Floor speeches on term limits (22 March 2016), executive immigration action (January and February 2015), Iran, Cuba and Guantanamo.

sources.title: CS/HB 5 (2022), Reducing Fetal and Infant Mortality, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 15 April 2022 (Ch. 2022-69): prohibits abortion after a set gestational age (15 weeks).

sources.title: CS/CS/SB 450 (2023), Death Penalty, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by the Governor (Ch. 2023-23): death sentences on a jury recommendation of fewer than unanimous jurors (eight of twelve).

sources.title: CS/CS/HB 1297 (2023), Capital Sexual Battery, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 2 May 2023 (Ch. 2023-25): death penalty for certain child sexual offenders.

sources.title: CS/SB 254 (2023), Treatments for Sex Reassignment, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 18 May 2023 (Ch. 2023-90): prohibits sex-reassignment prescriptions and procedures for patients under 18.

sources.title: CS/CS/HB 1069 (2023), Education, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 18 May 2023 (Ch. 2023-105): defines sex in the education code and sets title and pronoun rules.

sources.title: CS/CS/CS/SB 168 (2019), Federal Immigration Enforcement, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 17 June 2019 (Ch. 2019-102): bans sanctuary policies and requires support for federal immigration enforcement.

sources.title: SB 7072 (2021), Social Media Platforms, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Approved by Governor DeSantis 25 May 2021 (Ch. 2021-32): bars platforms from deplatforming candidates, with enforcement under state consumer law.

sources.title: CS/CS/HB 3 (2024), Online Protections for Minors, Florida Senate bill page (history, summary and Governor's approval)
sources.author: Florida Legislature
sources.usedFor: Ch. 2024-42: requires social media platforms to bar certain minors from creating accounts.

notes: First audit. Evidence is his Voteview record (2013-2018: about 100 roll calls searched by theme: health care, abortion, guns, immigration, trade, energy, Israel and Iran, debt and shutdown, taxes), the governor's own signings (the Heartbeat Protection Act release, the Parental Rights in Education release, and press accounts of HB 543, HB 1 and SB 1718) and his House floor speeches on the Stanford record (term limits, executive amnesty, Iran, Cuba, Guantanamo). MediaSum holds about 50 television and radio appearances (2013-2019, mostly Mueller, FISA and the Florida race); those hold no stated position on the test's statements beyond what is cited. His other signed Florida laws were read on the Florida Senate bill pages (history, summary, approval): HB 5, SB 450, HB 1297, SB 254, HB 1069, SB 168, SB 7072, HB 3; HB 7 (Stop WOKE Act, Ch. 2022-72), SB 266 (Ch. 2023-82) and the 2021 COVID-19 mandates law (HB 1-B, Ch. 2021-272) were read and match no statement of the test, so they settle none. House floor turns on the Fed, NSA, debt and taxes were searched (crec.js) and hold no position. Most statements are untouched by his record and stay null.
